newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU needs meaningful number of nations - Schmidhuber.
newsitem.headline: EMU needs meaningful number of nations - Schmidhuber.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Peter Schmidhuber said on Wednesday that European currency union should be postponed if a "critical mass" number of nations did not meet EMU entry criteria by early 1998.

"It makes no economic sense to start currency union with countries whose combined GDP is meaningless in overall EU terms," Schmidhuber said in a speech due to be given at a lawyers' conference in Berlin.
He went on to say that a smaller number of countries in currency union from the start would make technical and economic start-up problems easier to resolve.

"It is important for currency union that it begins with the right participants. A smaller number of participating nations would have the advantage of making technical and economic problems at the beginning easier to resolve," said Schmidhuber.
He added that only countries which had shown a past record of stability could be allowed into currency union in the first round.
"The first round of currency union should only be open to those countries that have shown themselves in the past to be prepared for the rigours of a strong stability policy," said Schmidhuber.
The inalterable precondition for the success of currency union was maintaining guaranteed stability.

"The new currency has to be able to prove itself as stable. Only then can the advantages of exchange rate and currency union be fully realised and the whole project be a political success," Schmidhuber said.
